log: 📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 2). You know dosages, preparations, contraindications. This is real medicine, just old.
📖 Your old life taught you things. 1 skill from your past — check your Journal.
Nothing here looks like home. You know none of these plants. Learn fast.
📖 Your hands remember: knap a Stone knife (stone + vine) — the oldest tool there is. Find the stone.
📖 Your hands remember: weave cloth (3 plant fiber — strip it from cleared brush), and build a Water Filter (cloth + charcoal from fire ashes). Dirty water doesn't have to stay dirty.

You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Omar Osei. Midwife. From Minneapolis, USA. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Dead Phone, Hard Candy, Field suture kit, Knife roll, Contract Quill. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. They found a deer this morning. Inside out. Not eaten — unmade. Like something was trying to understand how it worked. It didn't finish.
A woman, maybe 30s, with ink-stained fingers: "We've got days of stores, not weeks. The treeline is the pantry now. Learn what's out there."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.
🐞 SCENARIO: flashbulb moth. A dinner-plate moth, catching light wrong, four tiles east.
Walk toward it.
It spirals closer, wings catching light that isn't there. It's interested in you. Specifically you.
🦋 It moves.
It lands. It folds its wings. The light in them is building.
You don't know what that was. a moth the size of a dinner plate, catching light wrong Someone at the haven should hear about this.
⚔ A MOTH THE SIZE OF A DINNER PLATE, CATCHING LIGHT WRONG! You're on your own.
Turn-based now. Tap a tile to move — speed is squares. Then act.
It lands on a branch at eye level — wings half-open, catching light that isn't there. Watching you watch it.
You STRIKE the moth the size of a dinner plate, catching light wrong for 31 (Fire-hardened spear).
The moth the size of a dinner plate, catching light wrong falls.

Mostly wing. Crunchy. Tastes like dust and regret. It's dead. The carcass is there on the ground — search the body if you want the meat. But you don't know this flesh. Clean it, test it cautiously, or ask someone who knows. And don't leave it long: meat rots where it lies.
You clutch your Dead Phone, Hard Candy, Field suture kit, Knife roll, Contract Quill. You're still here.
